description: Settings of tools/diff_check.py (#309, D-847, D-848): the difference check between a source text and a proposed text. Python places the changed sentences by structure; whether a change is one of the declared kinds is one narrow question per kind to the registered JUDGE agent, decided from its probabilities (CHOICE-A). docs/fix/DIFF_CHECK_309.md.
enabled_note: Off as shipped (docs/fix/DIFF_CHECK_309.md section 1.3). With it off, write_run writes nothing. Switching it on needs no re-seal: no file of a sealed bundle reads this file.
threshold_note: D-855 (20 November 2026), from the accuracy pass external/s05/DIFF309_ACC/DIFF309_SWEEP.json: at 0.999, 20 of 22 real changes flagged, 2 false flags of 68 clean (misses: widened_scope 2 of 6). A development threshold read in-sample on the lane's own 24-pair accuracy set, never a bar. A question whose top answer is below it decides 'cannot be settled' (choice_decision.settle); null would settle nothing.
min_sentence_similarity_note: Share of two leftover sentences' words in common order (difflib ratio) above which a removed and an added sentence are one changed sentence; a tie is refused (version_changes._paired). Lower than version_changes' 0.6 because a dropped condition can remove a third of a sentence. Conventional, no evidence yet.

kinds.statement: The proposed text drops a condition, exception or qualification that the source text attached, so what the source text allowed or required only in some cases now applies without it.
A ban or duty that the source text placed on both or all parties is placed by the proposed text on one party only, so it now runs one way.
The proposed text widens the scope: what the source text said now covers more persons, things, places, periods or cases than before.
Something the source text made a party bound to do is, in the proposed text, only a statement of fact, intention or expectation, with no duty left.

red_line_statement: Party {party} holds this red line: "{quote}" The proposed text breaks this red line.
template:
A change to a text follows, then a statement about the change.

{passage_b}

STATEMENT
{passage_a}

Is the statement true of this change? Answer with one word.
Yes: the statement is true of the change.
No: it is not.
Unclear: the two texts do not let you decide.
replay_group_note: The replay's config is benchmark/baselines/choice_judge_prompt.json with its choice forms replaced by this file's one question and its first model group (Phi-4 on local_auditor at base, the JUDGE agent's model, JUDGE-AGENT-A) renamed to this group and agent; no model id is written here (diff_check.replay_config).
